The useful story is not the low price alone: AI agents may search, open pages, retry failed requests, and quietly run up a bill while completing a task. Explain how an agent turns a question into many behind-the-scenes web calls, then ask: Should AI agents need a spending limit before they can browse for us?

topic_candidates.title: OpenAI Says Its First Humanoid Robot Demo Could Arrive in 2027
topic_candidates.query: Sam Altman OpenAI humanoid robot cool demo 2027 October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Sam Altman confirmed that OpenAI plans to build a humanoid robot and said a “cool demo” could arrive in 2027, while suggesting useful robots walking around publicly are still farther away. The video should separate a promise from a product: a robot needs motors, balance, cameras, touch sensing, and software that turns perception into safe movement. End with: Is an AI lab building its own body the next big breakthrough—or just another demo race?
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Fresh coverage broke October 17–18, 2026, with AI Weekly reporting the confirmation and Fortune providing the underlying interview context. Robotics was also a strong current industry lane, while the supplied platform seeds favored futuristic technology and robots. This is likely the widest-reach story because it connects AI to homes, jobs, and physical machines, but it carries some hype risk because no robot has been shown. Estimated scores: discussion 9/10, accessibility 10/10, comments 9/10, visuals 10/10, evidence 8/10.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Explain the control problem: cameras estimate the world, software predicts what will happen, and motors constantly correct balance against gravity and changing surfaces.
